notes.title: Farewell North wins Best Video Game Soundtrack!
notes.notes:
Hiya folks,

I'm so happy to share that John Konsolakis took home the Best Video Game Soundtrack award for Farewell North last night at the Ivor Novello Awards! It was a truly special evening getting to celebrate his incredible work on such a grand stage and with such a prolific group of artists, from rock legends to pop icons, and I just continue to be blown away by the places Farewell North has taken us over this journey.

Thank you so much for all your support, and if you haven't given the [url=https://farewell-north.com/ost]soundtrack a listen then here's your reminder[/url]! John's work crafting the soundscape of Farewell North is truly special, and we're also tremendously grateful to Siobhan Miller and all the talented musicians, sound engineers and sound designers we had the pleasure of working with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38844242/80b7ef27d32809a51c347f900c04831f1a0fe566.png[/img]

Happy adventuring,
Kyle

notes.title: Farewell North is OUT NOW!
notes.notes:
[h1]Farewell North is OUT NOW![/h1]

For the past four years I've spent every single day working on this game; a deeply personal, atmospheric and emotional adventure about a woman and her dog saying farewell to the place they grew up. I'm so proud of what the team and I have created, and I'm absolutely thrilled to say that it's [b]out now[/b]!

The early press reviews have been so heartwarming, but it's [b][i]your[/i][/b] opinion that matters most, and I cannot wait to hear what you think. So, without further ado, I hope you'll join Chesley and Cailey on their adventures through the Scottish isles, and restore colour to their world! 

I have one more favour to ask of you though: once you've had a chance to play, please take a moment to leave a [b]review on Steam[/b]. Believe it or not, reviews are the best thing you can do to increase the chances that I'll get to do this all over again, and continue to make games.

Thank you for all the support these last four years, and enjoy Farewell North!

notes.title: Farewell North Release Update
notes.notes:
Hey folks!

I know you've been eagerly awaiting the release of Farewell North and, believe me, so have I! It still feels surreal that this journey is so close to coming to an end and I can't wait to get it out there for you. I do have some slightly bad news to share today, but don't worry, you will get to chase after sticks and herd some coos as our good boy Chesley very soon!

[b]Farewell North will now release on August 16th[/b]

As you may know, Steam is a super competitive market for indies. It's extremely hard to get visibility even on normal days, and I recently learned several other great indie games will all be releasing on the same day that I initially picked out for Farewell North. I've been pouring my heart and soul into this game for years now, and in hopes of giving it the best chance of finding its audience, I have decided to delay the release for only 1 day to [b]August 16th[/b].

I hope you understand and that this one additional day isn't too long of a wait!

-Kyle

notes.title: Release Date Announcement Trailer!
notes.notes:
Heya folks! 

It's been quite an adventure developing Farewell North these last four years. We're not quite at the finish line just yet, but I am thrilled to announce that Farewell North now has a release date - [b]August 15, 2024[/b]! 

With the release date announcement comes a brand new trailer with never before seen footage, and a few other big announcements as well - make sure you watch through to the end ;) 

I'm very delighted that with this trailer we're finally able to share the theme song for Farewell North, "My Heart's in the Highlands". Originally written by Robert Burns in 1789, "My Heart's in the Highlands" is the poem from which Farewell North takes its name. Our composer, [url=https://johnkonsolakis.eu/]John Konsolakis[/url], put together a modern rendition just for Farewell North featuring the voice of celebrated Scottish folk singer, [url=https://open.spotify.com/artist/1eIplU9Tirv31ciSwMlPrl?si=K6nHnU0gRAOhHxYyxAq8Eg]Siobhan Miller[/url]. 

This song isn't just for the trailer though! Together with John and Siobhan we've come up with a very special feature that I'm excited for you to discover for yourself in-game, so please look forward to that. 

[previewyoutube=OCa6c445rhU;full][/previewyoutube]

Anyways, now that we've got a date I've got work to do so I'd better get back to it! 

All the best, 
Kyle

notes.title: Devlog #33: Facial Animation and Introducing the Main Character
notes.notes:
One of the trickiest aspects of Farewell North's development has been bringing the main character to life in a way that players are able to relate and connect with her. I didn't realize it when I started development, but as a (mostly) solo indie dev it turns out that this is no small task, and for the past three years I've been doing everything I can to give her personality: animations, behaviours, voice acting, just to name a few. 

But something was always missing... 

In this devlog (the 33rd in the series!) I'll show you how I added eye tracking, lip sync and full facial animation to Farewell North, and finally reveal her name plus the meaning behind it. 

Enjoy! 

[previewyoutube=fkB3tK6zZSo;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Canoe and Accessibility Update!
notes.notes:
In this devlog you'll see how community feedback is being directly incorporated into the canoeing mechanic, making for a much more polished experience, and new accessibility options to help you enjoy Farewell North the way you'd like to experience it. 

On the canoe side, the animations have been greatly improved, though they're still not quite final. The colouring mechanic, where optimally timed paddle strokes bring colour rushing temporarily out of the canoe and increasing movement speed, has been overhauled to be much more visually interesting. 

New accessibility options have been added, including the ability to disable all visual aids for those who want a more explorative experience, and the ability to disable the canoe paddle timing requirement for those with motor impairments or who just prefer a more relaxed canoe gameplay. 

[previewyoutube=rlgSzrPHocE;full][/previewyoutube]

https://youtu.be/rlgSzrPHocE

notes.title: A new way to move color through the world!
notes.notes:
What a month! There's been so much progress on the game, it's hard to condense it down to a 10 minute devlog. First, I've been thinking a lot about the game mechanics and how they fit into puzzle gameplay. I realized that the demo (by the way, you can [url=https://farewell-north.com/discord]sign up to be a beta tester over on Discord[/url]!) doesn't currently have enough variety and movement in the gameplay, so I've introduced a new mechanic and a few new puzzle pieces to help mix it up. 

I also started implementing Photo Mode into the game over on Twitch! It's been a fun project to work on each stream, and something that I think is going to be a nice little bonus feature for the game. 

Finally, I've been reworking the jump mechanic and I'd love to hear your thoughts on the new system!

[previewyoutube=b29ExPgFNpI;full][/previewyoutube]

https://youtu.be/b29ExPgFNpI

notes.title: Improved Graphics, Perspective Puzzles and New Creepy Stuff!
notes.notes:
In the sixteenth (!) Farewell North devlog, we'll look at some big improvements to the game that have come out of the alpha playtests. 

Perspective puzzles have been massively improved to ensure they're understandable for new players, without going so far as to hold the players hand. They should be much more intuitive now, and some playtest footage shows we're on the right track here. 

The graphics of the uncoloured world have been significantly improved to ensure texture and shadow detail is still able to come through, and the results are quite substantial. 

See for yourself, and let me know what you think!

[previewyoutube=mHEOzCJxgzc;full][/previewyoutube]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mHEOzCJxgzc

notes.title: Stealth Update!
notes.notes:
In the eleventh Farewell North devlog, I'll show you how stealth is being integrated into the game!

Since I was a kid I've loved stealth games like Splinter Cell and Hitman, and more recently games like Dishonoured have scratched that itch. There's something about that genre that really just peaks my interest, and since day 1 I've been saying Farewell North would have stealth elements. It took a while to get to this part of the gameplay, but stealth is finally making its way into the game. 

I'm still quite adamant that Farewell North won't have any combat mechanics, so it was important to find a way to integrate the stealth into the gameplay in a way that actually fits within the mechanics and themes of the game. 

In this devlog I'll show you the main stealth gameplay loop, and explain how I'm thinking about stealth as a whole within the game. I'll also show you some effects I've been working on, and some behind-the-scenes in Unity where I've been working on vision cone that adjusts to the shape of the environment in real time. 

Check out the video here, and let me know what you think! 

[previewyoutube=w49kVuda5tk;full][/previewyoutube]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w49kVuda5tk
